rv.q: Ms. Kakoma’s spellbinding singing translates the songs’ appeal effortlessly.
But as a work of theater, “Dreaming Zenzile” struggles among the competing forms of recital, dream play, memory play and biography.
Yet somewhere in all that collaboration, Somi Kakoma’s bio-musical about the great South African singer Zenzile Miriam Makeba has slipped halfway through the cracks.
Overall, though, this bio-musical is an excellent one that feels fresh amid the many others on Broadway and beyond right now.
Dreaming Zenzile, while assuredly Kakoma’s homage, is also an opportunity to show off her magnificent voice.
As far as jukebox musicals go, Dreaming Zenzile earns a B-: plenty of musical gems decorating a rough book.
It's too bad that this fine artist's tumultuous life hasn't received more compelling treatment.
But Kakoma's dramaturgical chops are disastrously weak.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this Miriam Makeba tribute: while Somi Kakoma's vocal performance and charisma earn widespread praise, many find the musical structure underdeveloped and better suited as a concert than a biographical narrative.
